hyperedges.label: Main flow chain: idea to ship
Implement drives TDD and code review
Issue tracker templates for triage operations
Spec to Tickets to TDD Pipeline

nodes.label: Karpathy Guidelines
nodes.rationale: These guidelines bias toward caution over speed; for trivial tasks use judgment, not the full rigor.

nodes.label: Goal-Driven Execution
nodes.rationale: Strong success criteria let the LLM loop independently; weak criteria require constant clarification.

nodes.label: Anti-Pattern Examples
nodes.rationale: The 'overcomplicated' examples are not obviously wrong: the problem is timing, complexity added before it is needed.

nodes.label: Karpathy Guidelines Skill
nodes.rationale: Skill and CLAUDE.md and .cursor/rules must stay in sync so all surfaces ship identical principles.

nodes.label: Design Approval Gate
nodes.rationale: Even trivial projects must present a design and get approval: unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work on simple projects.

nodes.label: Clarifying Questions One at a Time
nodes.norm_label: clarifying questions one at a time

nodes.label: Brandkit Image Generation
nodes.rationale: A premium brand kit is not decoration; it is a visual argument for why the brand exists.

nodes.label: Industrial Brutalism & Tactical Telemetry UI
nodes.rationale: Pick ONE visual archetype per project and commit to it; never mix light and dark substrates within the same interface.

nodes.label: Caveman Communication Mode
nodes.rationale: Never invent abbreviations or arrows: measured zero token saving under the tokenizer, at the cost of decode clarity; full words are cheaper AND clearer.

nodes.label: Auto-Clarity
nodes.rationale: Drop caveman for security warnings, irreversible actions, and multi-step sequences where fragment order could be misread.

nodes.label: Design Taste Frontend (Anti-Slop)
nodes.rationale: Dials are baselines, never ask the user to edit the file; overrides happen conversationally, and the agent reads the brief before any design decision.

nodes.label: The Three Dials
nodes.rationale: DESIGN_VARIANCE / MOTION_INTENSITY / VISUAL_DENSITY are global variables every layout, motion, and density decision is gated by.

nodes.label: AI Tells / Forbidden Patterns
nodes.rationale: Em-dash is completely banned because it is the LLM's signature stylistic crutch and the #1 visual tell in production tests.

nodes.label: Motion Restraint & Micro-Interactions
nodes.rationale: Add the smallest set of motion moments that clarify state or hierarchy; avoid endless decorative loops, keep the interface from turning into a motion demo.

nodes.label: Design Point of View & Craft
nodes.rationale: The goal is not just to make it nicer; ship working code with a clear design point of view, strong craft, and product detail for the user's actual context.

nodes.label: Game Development Orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Decision rule: start with a State Machine and add ECS only when performance demands it.

nodes.label: 2D Game Development
nodes.rationale: 2D is about clarity. Every pixel should communicate.

nodes.label: 3D Game Development
nodes.rationale: 3D is about illusion. Create the impression of detail, not the detail itself.

nodes.label: Rendering Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Culling and LOD avoid rendering what is not visible; simple colliders with complex visuals.

nodes.label: Game Art
nodes.rationale: Art serves gameplay. If it doesn't help the player, it's decoration.

nodes.label: Art Style Selection
nodes.rationale: Style choice trades production speed, skill floor, and scalability (pixel art, PBR 3D, low-poly, cel-shaded).

nodes.label: Asset Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Create at source resolution, scale down never up; pick a base unit and stick to it.

nodes.label: Game Audio
nodes.rationale: 50% of the game experience is audio. A muted game loses half its soul.

nodes.label: Audio Category System
nodes.rationale: Priority hierarchy decides which sounds survive channel contention: voice over SFX over music over ambient.

nodes.label: Game Design
nodes.rationale: Fun is discovered through iteration, not designed on paper.

nodes.label: Core Loop
nodes.rationale: Every game needs a fun 30-second loop: ACTION, FEEDBACK, REWARD, REPEAT.

nodes.label: Player Psychology
nodes.rationale: Bartle-style motivation types and reward schedules (fixed, variable, ratio) shape retention.

nodes.label: Difficulty Balancing
nodes.rationale: Flow state: too hard frustrates, too easy bores; dynamic/selection/accessibility balancing keeps engagement.

nodes.label: Mobile Game Development
nodes.rationale: Mobile is the most constrained platform. Respect battery and attention.

nodes.label: Touch Input
nodes.rationale: Minimum touch target 44x44 points; touch is imprecise and occludes the screen.

nodes.label: Multiplayer
nodes.rationale: Never trust the client. The server is the source of truth.

nodes.label: Network Architecture
nodes.rationale: Dedicated server vs host-based vs P2P trades latency, cost, and security.

nodes.label: Lag Compensation
nodes.rationale: Prediction, interpolation, and reconciliation make the game playable at 100-200ms latency.

nodes.label: Bandwidth Reduction
nodes.rationale: Delta compression, quantization, priority, and area of interest send only what is necessary.

nodes.label: PC/Console Game Development
nodes.rationale: Engine is a tool. Master the principles, then adapt to any engine.

nodes.label: Engine Selection
nodes.rationale: Unity 6 vs Godot 4 vs Unreal 5: choose by project needs (2D/3D, team size, cost), not hype.

nodes.label: Input Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Map ACTIONS, not buttons, so one mapping works across Xbox/PS/Nintendo layouts.

nodes.label: Profiling
nodes.rationale: Profile early and often; fix draw calls, GC spikes, physics, and shader bottlenecks.

nodes.label: VR/AR Development
nodes.rationale: Comfort is not optional. Sick players don't play.

nodes.label: Comfort Principles
nodes.rationale: Teleport/snap turn, vignettes, and player-controlled cameras prevent motion sickness.

nodes.label: Frame Budget
nodes.rationale: VR requires consistent frame times; 90 FPS = 11.11ms budget; a single dropped frame is visible judder.

nodes.label: Hand Tracking
nodes.rationale: More immersive but less precise; good for social/casual, challenging for action.

nodes.label: Web Browser Game Development
nodes.rationale: Browser is the most accessible platform. Respect its constraints.

nodes.label: Web Framework Selection
nodes.rationale: Phaser/PixiJS for 2D, Babylon.js/Three.js for 3D; raw Canvas/WebGL for custom.

nodes.label: WebGPU
nodes.rationale: New projects use WebGPU with WebGL fallback; detect via navigator.gpu.

nodes.label: GDScript 2.0
nodes.rationale: Type all variables for performance gains; typed arrays; yield replaced by await.

nodes.label: Tween System
nodes.rationale: Tween node is deprecated; use create_tween() in code.

nodes.label: Annotations
nodes.rationale: export/onready/tool keywords become @export/@onready/@tool modifiers.

nodes.label: Signal Callables
nodes.rationale: String-based connections are discouraged; use callables and signal objects.

nodes.label: queue_free
nodes.rationale: Always use queue_free() instead of free() so nodes are freed at a safe time; check is_instance_valid() before access.

nodes.label: Node Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Clearing children by iterating a live array breaks indices; use while-loop, duplicate() copy, or clear_children() (Godot 4.1+).

nodes.label: Godot CLI
nodes.rationale: Enables running games, exporting projects, running scripts, debugging, and CI/CD automation.

nodes.label: Signals
nodes.rationale: Signals decouple nodes; preferred over direct references.

nodes.label: Autoload
nodes.rationale: Register scripts in Project → Autoload for global access; home for global state and game management.

nodes.label: GDScript
nodes.rationale: Reference library covering basics, advanced features, exports, static typing, warnings.

nodes.label: Scene Instantiation
nodes.rationale: preload() for frequently used scenes, threaded loading for large scenes.

nodes.label: Object Pooling
nodes.rationale: Reuse pooled scene instances to avoid allocation churn and GC.

nodes.label: Anchor Layout
nodes.rationale: UI layout is anchor- and offset-based with presets for full-rect, center, top-left.

nodes.label: to_dict/from_dict Pattern
nodes.rationale: Keep save data explicit in Dictionaries rather than serializing engine objects directly.

nodes.label: Save/Load Game State
nodes.rationale: FileAccess + JSON.stringify to user:// saves; create_from_dict for reconstruction.

nodes.label: Godot Singleton Pattern
nodes.rationale: Minimize singleton use and keep single responsibility per singleton.

nodes.label: GameManager
nodes.rationale: Global game state (state, score, lives) managed through a singleton with static get_instance().

nodes.label: TSCN File Structure
nodes.rationale: Five sections in order: file descriptor, external resources, internal resources, nodes, connections.

nodes.label: Timestamp Best Practices
nodes.rationale: Explicit precision (seconds vs milliseconds), use DateTime objects over raw timestamps, handle timezone conversion for user-visible times, and add error handling when parsing external timestamps.

nodes.label: Python-Driven True Randomization
nodes.rationale: LLMs always pick the first layout option; a simulated deterministic Python random.choice() run in the design_plan forces varied hero/typography/component/GSAP selections so the same UI is never defaulted to twice.

nodes.label: Hero Line Limit
nodes.rationale: Narrow containers produce 6-line wrapped headings; ultra-wide H1 containers with clamp() font sizing guarantee 2-3 lines maximum so the hero breathes.

nodes.label: Image-First Workflow
nodes.rationale: The generated image is the design source and the code is the translation layer; freeform coding first produces generic reinterpretations, so generation must precede analysis which must precede implementation.

nodes.label: Deep Image Analysis
nodes.rationale: Images are treated as a design specification: extract exact text, type scale, spacing relationships, color logic and component behavior before coding, otherwise implementation drifts into generic defaults.

nodes.label: Section Image Generation
nodes.rationale: One section = one large readable image; compressed boards shrink text below analyzability and cropping old images destroys spacing, proportions and type-scale relationships, so fresh standalone regeneration is preferred.

nodes.label: Hero Minimalism
nodes.rationale: The first viewport must stay calm and readable on a small laptop; overcrowding it with pills, fake stats and micro-labels destroys hierarchy.

nodes.label: App Design Bible
nodes.rationale: Locking palette, type, spacing, radius, icon and navigation rules before generating a multi-screen set prevents screens 3-5 drifting into a different app.

nodes.label: One-Image-Per-Section Rule
nodes.rationale: Collapsing multiple sections into one frame shrinks text, buttons and spacing below analyzable size; each horizontal section image must stay a high-fidelity reference a coding model can rebuild from.

nodes.label: Hero Composition Bias
nodes.rationale: Left-text/right-image is the most overused AI hero pattern; it must be a deliberate choice, not the default reflex, with composition anchors varied across the page.

nodes.label: Anti-AI-Tell Removal
nodes.rationale: A few decisive fixes beat broad cosmetic churn: purple-blue glow gradients, generic 3-card rows, oversized rounded cards and empty marketing adjectives are the highest-impact tells to remove while preserving the user's intent.

nodes.label: Analog Degradation Effects
nodes.rationale: Halftone dithering, CRT scanlines and mechanical noise simulate physical hardware limitations so the interface reads as real machinery rather than purely digital output.

nodes.label: Banned Output Patterns
nodes.rationale: Placeholder comments, skeleton structures and 'rest follows the same pattern' prose are hard failures because a partial output is a broken output in production-critical work.

nodes.label: Clean Breakpoint Pausing
nodes.rationale: When approaching the token limit, write at full quality to a clean breakpoint and emit a [PAUSED - X of Y complete] marker so 'continue' resumes exactly, without compressing or skipping sections.

nodes.label: Completeness Discipline
nodes.rationale: Optimize for completeness, not brevity: lock the deliverable count upfront, generate everything, then cross-check the output against the original request before responding.

nodes.label: The Ladder
nodes.rationale: Stop at the first rung that holds (YAGNI, codebase reuse, stdlib, native platform, installed dep, one line, minimum code); laziness shortens the solution, never the reading of the problem.

nodes.label: YAGNI
nodes.rationale: Speculative need should be skipped: the best code is the code never written, and abstractions without a second user or config nobody sets are deleted, not scaffolded.

nodes.label: ponytail: Comment Convention
nodes.rationale: Deliberate simplifications are marked with a ponytail: comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path so a shortcut reads as intent rather than ignorance and can be revisited.

nodes.label: Debt Ledger
nodes.rationale: Harvesting every ponytail: comment into one ledger prevents a deliberate deferral from quietly becoming permanent; markers without a named trigger are flagged as rot risk.

nodes.label: Benchmark Scoreboard
nodes.rationale: Figures are published benchmark medians, never per-repo savings, because the unbuilt version was never written so there is no real baseline to subtract from in a live repo.

nodes.label: Fix Priority
nodes.rationale: Apply font swap first (biggest instant improvement, lowest risk), then palette cleanup, interaction states, layout, components, missing states and typography polish for maximum impact with minimum risk.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md
nodes.rationale: The ubiquitous-language document that helps agents decode project jargon; defines domain terms (Issue tracker, Issue, Decision ticket, Triage role) and flagged ambiguities so agents stop using 20 words where 1 will do.

nodes.label: Issue tracker
nodes.rationale: The tool that hosts a repo's issues (GitHub Issues, Linear, local .scratch/ markdown). The terms backlog and backlog backend/manager were collapsed into this single issue tracker term.

nodes.label: Issue
nodes.rationale: A single tracked unit of work inside an Issue tracker; the word ticket is avoided except when quoting external systems or for Decision tickets.

nodes.label: Decision ticket
nodes.rationale: A wayfinder unit: a child Issue of a wayfinder:map holding a question whose resolution is a decision, not a slice of a build to execute; the decision qualifier is what keeps it distinct from an implementation ticket.

nodes.label: Triage role
nodes.rationale: A canonical state-machine label applied to an Issue during triage (e.g. needs-triage, ready-for-afk); each role maps to a real label string in the Issue tracker via docs/agents/triage-labels.md.

nodes.label: Skill bucket layout
nodes.rationale: engineering/ and productivity/ are the promoted buckets (every skill there needs a README reference and plugin entry); misc/, personal/, in-progress/, and deprecated/ are kept but never promoted or documented.

nodes.label: ask-matt router
nodes.rationale: The router that maps every user-reachable skill and how they relate; any add/rename/remove/flow change must trigger an ask-matt re-check, because a stale router is a router that lies.

nodes.label: Installation paths (plugin vs skills.sh)
nodes.rationale: Two philosophies: the Claude Code plugin subscribes to a managed read-only bundle; skills.sh copies editable files you own. Pick one - installing both leaves you with every skill twice.

nodes.label: Grilling session
nodes.rationale: The fix for failure mode #1 (the agent didn't do what I want): getting the agent to ask detailed questions before building closes the communication gap between you and the agent.

nodes.label: Shared language
nodes.rationale: The fix for failure mode #2 (the agent is way too verbose): a CONTEXT.md document decoding project jargon; with consistent naming, codebases become easier to navigate and the agent spends fewer tokens thinking.

nodes.label: Feedback loops
nodes.rationale: The fix for failure mode #3 (the code doesn't work): static types, browser access, and a red-green-refactor test loop so the agent is never flying blind; implemented as the /tdd and /diagnosing-bugs skills.

nodes.label: Deep module design
nodes.rationale: The fix for failure mode #4 (we built a ball of mud): agents accelerate software entropy, so caring about code design is built into every layer; /to-spec quizzes module scope and /improve-codebase-architecture rescues messy codebases.

nodes.label: Wayfinder (decision mapping flow)
nodes.rationale: Renamed from decision-mapping: charts a route through a foggy problem (fog of war, frontier, the map). Plan, don't do - the map produces decisions, not deliverables; destination is the leading word; claim by assignment, native blocking, HITL/AFK classification, and a fourth task ticket type for manual work.

nodes.label: Wayfinder map
nodes.rationale: The map is an index, not a store: a single wayfinder:map issue whose child issues are the tickets; a decision lives in exactly one place. Collaborative by default - moved off local Markdown onto the repo's issue tracker, tracker-agnostic behind a pointer.

nodes.label: Blocking edges
nodes.rationale: Tracer-bullet tickets each declare their blocking edges; a local file writes them as text, a real tracker as native blocking links so the frontier is visible and several agents can run in parallel.

nodes.label: Code review (Fowler smell baseline)
nodes.rationale: Promoted from in-progress/ to engineering/ with an always-on Fowler smell baseline (~12 high-signal Bad Smells in Code); a documented repo standard overrides the baseline and every smell is a judgement call, never a hard violation.

nodes.label: Grilling confirmation gate and facts-vs-decisions
nodes.rationale: A confirmation gate stops the agent from enacting the plan until shared understanding is confirmed, and grilling splits facts (look them up) from decisions (put each to the human) so a grilling agent never races ahead and answers its own questions.

nodes.label: User-invoked vs model-invoked split
nodes.rationale: User-invoked skills are reachable only by the human (disable-model-invocation + policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false) with human-facing descriptions stripped of trigger lists; model-invoked skills keep rich trigger phrasing. A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked skills, never another user-invoked one.

nodes.label: Prose-invocation dependencies
nodes.rationale: Dependencies are expressed as /skill-style prose invocation, not deep cross-folder file links; shared reference docs live inside the owning skill and others reach them by invoking the skill.

nodes.label: Docs page (aihero.dev distributed router)
nodes.rationale: Every promoted skill gets a human-facing docs page at docs/<bucket>/<skill-name>.md published at aihero.dev/skills-<name>; its job is to relieve the cognitive load of remembering user-invoked skills - the pages are collectively a distributed router, each a node, with every link absolute.

nodes.label: Leading word surfacing
nodes.rationale: The non-negotiable of a docs page is surfacing the skill's leading word / defining idea (deep module, tracer bullet, red-green) - it pays off twice: the reader learns what the skill is and the word they'll later think with to reach for it.

nodes.label: ADR 0001: Explicit setup pointer only for hard dependencies
nodes.norm_label: adr 0001: explicit setup pointer only for hard dependencies

nodes.label: setup-matt-pocock-skills (per-repo config seeder)
nodes.rationale: Seeds per-repo config (issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, domain doc layout) that engineering skills depend on; run once per repo before using the other engineering skills.

nodes.label: Hard vs soft dependency split
nodes.rationale: Hard dependencies (to-tickets, to-spec, triage) get an explicit run /setup-matt-pocock-skills pointer because without the mapping output is wrong; soft dependencies (diagnose, tdd, improve-codebase-architecture) degrade gracefully. The split keeps soft skills token-light and avoids cargo-culting the setup pointer where it isn't load-bearing.

nodes.label: ADR 0002: Ship as Claude Code plugin
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002: ship as claude code plugin

nodes.label: Claude Code plugin distribution
nodes.rationale: plugin.json accepts an explicit array of skill paths, so the promoted set can be listed one by one with zero ambiguity; marketplace.json makes the repo its own single-plugin marketplace; version stays synced with package.json because Claude uses plugin version to decide when updates appear.

nodes.label: Codex plugin (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Codex's manifest accepts skills only as a single path string and drops symlinks on install, so a curated promoted-only path needs either restructuring skills/ or committing duplicate copies - both structural decisions deferred until Codex supports arrays or preserves symlinks; skills.sh remains the universal installer for Codex today.

nodes.label: Promoted skill set
nodes.rationale: Only engineering/ and productivity/ skills ship; misc/, personal/, in-progress/, and deprecated/ are deliberately never promoted, which is what forces the curated plugin selection.

nodes.label: Changesets versioning tooling
nodes.rationale: This folder is auto-generated by @changesets/cli, a build tool that versions and publishes code for single- or multi-package repos.

nodes.label: Wayfinder routing guidance in ask-matt
nodes.rationale: Sharpens two routing mistakes: over-reaching for wayfinder (it's the heaviest, most cognitively demanding flow - a well-scoped feature belongs on /grill-with-docs) and losing the way at handoff (wayfinder hands off to /to-spec, which collapses the map's linked decisions into a buildable plan, not straight to /implement).

nodes.label: Codex skill metadata (agents/openai.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Adds agents/openai.yaml beside every SKILL.md (interface.display_name, short_description) so the set works in both harnesses without generated copies; policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false is the Codex analog of disable-model-invocation, and AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Local markdown tracker
nodes.rationale: One file per ticket under .scratch/<feature>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md, never a single combined tickets.md; the spec file is spec.md (not PRD.md) to match /to-spec. Setup is friendlier: triage labels asked only when triage is installed, external-PR flag defaults off, domain docs default to single-context.

nodes.label: Grilling general-use scope
nodes.rationale: Reworded grilling so it is no longer scoped to a software plan (this plan to this, exploring the codebase to exploring the environment); the technique is unchanged but now reads as a stress-test of any plan, decision, or idea.

nodes.label: Prototype as primary source
nodes.rationale: The prototype is captured as runnable evidence on a throwaway prototype/<name> branch out of main with a context pointer left on the implementation issue, instead of being deleted - main keeps only the validated decision while exploration stays findable; the verdict is still captured in an issue/ADR/commit.

nodes.label: Single-plugin marketplace
nodes.rationale: The repo is its own single-plugin marketplace so you can subscribe to the promoted skills as a managed read-only bundle instead of copying editable files; skills.sh remains the universal installer and the path for Codex and other harnesses.

nodes.label: Wayfinder decision ticket term
nodes.rationale: People kept reading wayfinder tickets as implementation tickets, so the unit is named a decision ticket - a question whose resolution is a decision; CONTEXT.md records it as a domain term so the avoid: ticket guidance no longer contradicts wayfinder's deliberate use of the word.

nodes.label: Wayfinder research subagents
nodes.rationale: Because research is AFK, charting doesn't stop and read it: after creating the tickets, the charting session fires a /research subagent per research ticket to burn it down in parallel, capturing findings on a throwaway research/<name> branch with a context pointer; research tickets are the one exception to one-ticket-per-session.

nodes.label: YAGNI scoping filter
nodes.rationale: The Explore step of improve-codebase-architecture scopes to where change is actually landing: if you name a direction it takes it, otherwise it reads the last ~20 commit messages to bias toward actively-developed paths - a deepening opportunity in code nobody touches is a refactor you'll never cash in.

nodes.label: Mainstream issue trackers only
nodes.rationale: Each issue-tracker backend hard-codes a CLI shape into the skills (commands, flags, output parsing) - permanent maintenance surface that must keep working and keep being tested, so first-class support is only worth it for mainstream trackers; escape hatches (local markdown, other/custom) cover non-mainstream tools.

nodes.label: Open-ended grilling (no question caps)
nodes.rationale: Grilling is intentionally open-ended until every branch of the decision tree is resolved - a fixed cap cuts off useful exploration on hard problems or feels arbitrary on easy ones, and would conflate under-specified plans (working as intended) with redundant questions (a prompt-quality issue); natural-language steering is the intended control surface.

nodes.label: No verify mode for setup-matt-pocock-skills
nodes.rationale: A verify flag or sibling skill would duplicate what the prompt-driven setup skill already handles in conversation (run /setup-matt-pocock-skills and tell it to verify your current setup), and would risk two skills drifting apart as seed templates evolve.

nodes.label: Design An Interface
nodes.rationale: Deprecated (rationale: superseded by codebase-design's DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md, which carries the same Design-It-Twice parallel sub-agent pattern inside the maintained skill that owns the deep-module vocabulary).

nodes.label: Design It Twice
nodes.rationale: Based on 'Design It Twice' from A Philosophy of Software Design (Ousterhout): your first idea is unlikely to be the best, so generate multiple radically different designs and compare.

nodes.label: Depth (interface evaluation)
nodes.rationale: Depth criterion from A Philosophy of Software Design: small interface hiding significant complexity = deep module (good); large interface with thin implementation = shallow module (avoid).

nodes.label: QA Session
nodes.rationale: Deprecated (rationale: interactive QA issue-filing was folded into the triage workflow, which moves incoming issues through triage roles and produces agent-ready issues for implement to pick up).

nodes.label: Issue Filing
nodes.rationale: Issues must be durable and written from the user's perspective: no file paths or line numbers (they go stale), describe behaviours not code, use the project's domain language, reproduction steps mandatory.

nodes.label: Issue Breakdown
nodes.rationale: Break a report into many thin issues over few thick ones — each independently fixable and verifiable, marked with honest blocking relationships, filed in dependency order to maximise parallelism.

nodes.label: Request Refactor Plan
nodes.rationale: Deprecated (rationale: refactoring now runs through the main flow — grill-with-docs → to-spec → to-tickets → implement — where plans become tracer-bullet tickets rather than a single refactor-plan GitHub issue).

nodes.label: Tiny Commits Plan
nodes.rationale: Martin Fowler's advice: make each refactoring step as small as possible so you can always see the program working; every commit leaves the codebase in a working state.

nodes.label: Refactor Plan Issue Template
nodes.rationale: The plan issue records problem, solution, commits, a decision document, testing decisions, outdated-scope and further notes — but never specific file paths or code snippets, which go stale quickly.

nodes.label: Ubiquitous Language Glossary
nodes.rationale: Deprecated (rationale: superseded by domain-modeling, the active discipline that keeps CONTEXT.md a clean glossary and records decisions in ADRs; ubiquitous-language was its stateless, conversation-only predecessor. Also disable-model-invocation: true).

nodes.label: Canonical Terms
nodes.rationale: Be opinionated: when multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others as aliases to avoid; only include terms with domain meaning.

nodes.label: Flagged Ambiguities
nodes.rationale: Flag ambiguous or overloaded terms explicitly (e.g. 'account' meaning both Customer and User) with a clear recommended resolution; keep definitions tight and show relationships and cardinality.

nodes.label: Skill Invocation Models
nodes.rationale: Two invocation modes: user-invoked (disable-model-invocation: true, or policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false in agents/openai.yaml) versus model-invoked (rich trigger phrasing so the model can reach for them).

nodes.label: Ask Matt Router
nodes.rationale: You don't remember every skill, so ask: most paths run along one main flow, two on-ramps merge onto it, everything else is standalone or a vocabulary layer that runs underneath.

nodes.label: Main Flow: idea to ship
nodes.rationale: Context hygiene: keep grilling, spec and tickets in one unbroken context window — don't compact or clear until after /to-tickets; each /implement then starts fresh, working from the ticket.

nodes.label: On-ramp
nodes.rationale: A starting situation that generates work, then merges onto the main flow; triage is only for issues you didn't create, because /to-tickets output is already agent-ready.

nodes.label: Smart Zone
nodes.rationale: The window (~120k tokens on state-of-the-art models) within which the model still reasons sharply; if a session approaches it before /to-tickets, handoff and continue in a fresh thread rather than pushing on degraded.

nodes.label: Handoff
nodes.rationale: Compacts the conversation into a markdown file you open in a fresh session — the bridge between context windows, in either direction; it forks, whereas the built-in /compact continues in the same conversation.

nodes.label: Code Review (two-axis)
nodes.rationale: Two axes are reported separately on purpose: a change can pass one axis and fail the other, and merging or reranking would let one axis mask the other.

nodes.label: Fowler Smell Baseline
nodes.rationale: A fixed set of Fowler code smells (Refactoring ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing; repo standards override it, each smell is a judged heuristic (e.g. possible Feature Envy), never a hard violation.

nodes.label: Fixed Point
nodes.rationale: Confirm the fixed point resolves and the diff is non-empty before spawning the two parallel sub-agents — a bad ref or empty diff fails here, not inside the sub-agents.

nodes.label: Codebase Design
nodes.rationale: Consistent vocabulary is the whole point — don't substitute component/service/API/boundary. Rejected framings: depth-as-line-ratio (rewards padding the implementation), interface-as-keyword (too narrow), boundary (overloaded with DDD's bounded context).

nodes.label: Deep Module
nodes.rationale: A lot of behaviour behind a small interface at a clean seam — a module is deep when a large amount of behaviour sits behind a small interface, shallow when the interface is nearly as complex as the implementation.

nodes.label: Interface
nodes.rationale: Everything a caller must know to use the module correctly: the type signature plus invariants, ordering constraints, error modes, required configuration, and performance characteristics.

nodes.label: Seam
nodes.rationale: Michael Feathers: a place where you can alter behaviour without editing in that place; the location at which a module's interface lives. Avoid 'boundary' (overloaded with DDD's bounded context).

nodes.label: Adapter
nodes.rationale: A concrete thing that satisfies an interface at a seam; describes role (what slot it fills), not substance (what's inside). One adapter means a hypothetical seam; two adapters means a real one.

nodes.label: Depth
nodes.rationale: Leverage at the interface: the amount of behaviour a caller or test can exercise per unit of interface they have to learn; depth is a property of the interface, not the implementation.

nodes.label: Leverage
nodes.rationale: What callers get from depth: more capability per unit of interface they learn; one implementation pays back across N call sites and M tests.

nodes.label: Locality
nodes.rationale: What maintainers get from depth: change, bugs, knowledge, and verification concentrate in one place rather than spreading across callers — fix once, fixed everywhere.

nodes.label: Deletion Test
nodes.rationale: Imagine deleting the module: if complexity vanishes it was a pass-through; if complexity reappears across N callers it was earning its keep.

nodes.label: Dependency Categories
nodes.rationale: Classify a deepening candidate's dependencies: in-process (always deepenable, no adapter), local-substitutable (test stand-in exists), remote-but-owned (ports & adapters), true external (injected port, mock adapter).

nodes.label: Seam Discipline
nodes.rationale: One adapter means a hypothetical seam, two adapters means a real one — don't introduce a port unless at least two adapters are justified; keep internal seams private, don't expose them through the interface just because tests use them.

nodes.label: Replace, Don't Layer Testing
nodes.rationale: Old unit tests on shallow modules become waste once tests at the deepened module's interface exist — delete them; tests should survive internal refactors and describe behaviour, not implementation.

nodes.label: Design It Twice (parallel interfaces)
nodes.rationale: Based on 'Design It Twice' (Ousterhout): spawn 3+ parallel sub-agents each with a separate technical brief and a different design constraint, then present sequentially, compare by depth, locality and seam placement, and give an opinionated recommendation or hybrid.

nodes.label: Diagnosing Bugs
nodes.rationale: A discipline for hard bugs and performance regressions: reproduce → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test → cleanup + post-mortem; skip phases only when explicitly justified.

nodes.label: Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 is the skill — everything else is mechanical: no red-capable, deterministic, fast, agent-runnable command that goes red on this bug means no hypothesising. Jumping straight to a hypothesis is the exact failure this skill prevents.

nodes.label: Tight Loop
nodes.rationale: Treat the loop as a product: make it faster, sharper (assert the specific symptom, not 'didn't crash') and more deterministic; a 2-second deterministic loop is a debugging superpower; raise flaky-bug reproduction rate until debuggable.

nodes.label: Regression Test
nodes.rationale: Write the regression test before the fix, but only if a correct seam exists; the minimised repro becomes the clean regression test.

nodes.label: Correct Seam
nodes.rationale: A seam where the test exercises the real bug pattern as it occurs at the call site; if no correct seam exists, that itself is the finding — the architecture is preventing the bug from being locked down.

nodes.label: ADR (Architecture Decision Record)
nodes.rationale: An ADR can be a single paragraph — the value is in recording that a decision was made and why, not in filling out sections; ADRs live in docs/adr/ with sequential numbering, created lazily.

nodes.label: ADR Criteria
nodes.rationale: Offer an ADR only when all three hold: hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off; covers architectural shape, integration patterns, lock-in tech, boundary decisions, and deliberate deviations.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md Glossary
nodes.rationale: Be opinionated (pick the best term, list the rest under _Avoid_), keep definitions to one or two sentences, and only include project-specific domain terms — general programming concepts don't belong.

nodes.label: CONTEXT-MAP.md
nodes.rationale: For multi-context repos the root CONTEXT-MAP.md lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate (e.g. event-driven relationships); the skill infers single vs multi-context structure.

nodes.label: Domain Modeling
nodes.rationale: Active discipline: challenge terms, invent edge cases, write glossary and decisions the moment they crystallise. CONTEXT.md is a glossary and nothing else — no implementation details. Offer ADRs sparingly: only when hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md
nodes.rationale: Pure glossary of canonical terms, updated inline as terms are resolved; never a spec or implementation scratch pad.

nodes.label: ADR
nodes.rationale: Architecture Decision Record at docs/adr/; created lazily and only when all three criteria hold: hard to reverse, surprising without context, real trade-off.

nodes.label: Grill with Docs
nodes.rationale: Relentless interview that sharpens a plan while creating docs (ADRs and glossary) as it goes — grilling plus domain-modeling combined.

nodes.label: TDD
nodes.rationale: Use TDD where possible, at pre-agreed seams; typecheck and single test files run regularly, full suite once at the end.

nodes.label: Improve Codebase Architecture
nodes.rationale: Aim is testability and AI-navigability. Scope before you scan (YAGNI) — weight recently-changed hot spots from commit history. HTML report goes to the OS temp dir so nothing lands in the repo.

nodes.label: Deepening Opportunity
nodes.rationale: Refactors that turn shallow modules into deep ones, found by exploring where understanding requires bouncing between small modules.

nodes.label: Deletion Test
nodes.rationale: Would deleting the module concentrate complexity, or just move it? A 'yes, concentrates' answer is the signal for a deepening opportunity.

nodes.label: Codebase Design
nodes.rationale: Provides the shared architecture vocabulary (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) and principles like the deletion test and 'one adapter = hypothetical seam, two = real'.

nodes.label: HTML Report Format
nodes.rationale: Self-contained HTML file using Tailwind and Mermaid from CDNs; mix Mermaid graphs with hand-built divs/SVG so reports don't look generic.

nodes.label: Codebase Design Glossary
nodes.rationale: Report must use exactly the /codebase-design vocabulary (module, interface, implementation, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality); never 'component', 'service', 'API' or 'boundary'.

nodes.label: Diagram Patterns
nodes.rationale: Mermaid graphs for dependency/call flow, hand-built boxes-and-arrows for deep-module weight, cross-sections for layered shallowness, mass diagrams for interface-as-wide-as-implementation, call-graph collapse. Variety is part of the point.

nodes.label: Prototype
nodes.rationale: A prototype is throwaway code that answers a question; the question decides the shape (logic vs UI). Rules: throwaway from day one, one command to run, no persistence, skip polish, surface the state, capture as a primary source on a throwaway branch.

nodes.label: Primary Source Capture
nodes.rationale: The prototype itself is committed to a throwaway branch as a primary source with a context pointer on the issue; main keeps only the validated decision.

nodes.label: Logic Prototype Branch
nodes.rationale: Tiny interactive terminal app to drive a state model by hand; for questions about business logic, state transitions, or data shape.

nodes.label: Portable Logic Module
nodes.rationale: Logic sits behind a small pure interface (reducer, state machine, pure functions, or method surface) so it can be lifted into the real codebase; the TUI is throwaway, the logic module isn't.

nodes.label: TUI Shell
nodes.rationale: Lightweight terminal UI that re-renders the whole frame each tick; a thin shell over the pure module, never shipped to production.

nodes.label: UI Prototype Branch
nodes.rationale: Several radically different UI variations on a single route, switchable from a floating bottom bar; user flips between variants, steals bits, throws the rest away.

nodes.label: Variant
nodes.rationale: Variants must be structurally different (layout, hierarchy, primary affordance), not just different colours; default 3, cap 5. Share little code between them.

nodes.label: Prototype Switcher
nodes.rationale: Floating bottom bar with prev/next arrows and variant label; updates the ?variant= URL search param, arrow-key navigable, hidden in production builds.

nodes.label: Sub-Shape A
nodes.rationale: Preferred: variants rendered on an existing page gated by ?variant=, keeping real data, params and auth. Variants are much easier to judge butting up against the rest of the app; an empty throwaway route is a vacuum that hides design problems.

nodes.label: Research
nodes.rationale: Spin up a background agent so you keep working while it reads; findings captured as one Markdown file in the repo, matching the existing notes convention.

nodes.label: Primary Sources
nodes.rationale: Investigate against official docs, source code, specs, first-party APIs — not secondary write-ups; follow every claim back to the source that owns it.

nodes.label: Resolving Merge Conflicts
nodes.rationale: Preserve both intents where possible; where incompatible, pick the one matching the merge's stated goal and note the trade-off. Never invent behaviour; always resolve, never --abort.

nodes.label: Primary Sources
nodes.rationale: Understand deeply why each change was made: read commit messages, PRs, original issues/tickets to recover original intent before resolving each hunk.

nodes.label: Automated Checks
nodes.rationale: Discover and run the project's automated checks — typically typecheck, then tests, then format — and fix anything the merge broke.

nodes.label: Setup Matt Pocock Skills
nodes.rationale: Prompt-driven skill, not a deterministic script: explore, present findings, confirm, write. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills; re-running only needed to switch trackers or restart.

nodes.label: Issue Tracker
nodes.rationale: Where issues live (GitHub by default, GitLab, local markdown, or other); skills like to-tickets, triage, to-spec and qa read from and write to it. Recorded in docs/agents/issue-tracker.md.

nodes.label: Triage Labels
nodes.rationale: Five canonical roles with label strings equal to their names: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix. Written only when the triage skill is installed.

nodes.label: docs/agents
nodes.rationale: Where the skill's prior output lives: issue-tracker.md, domain.md, triage-labels.md; an ## Agent skills block is added to CLAUDE.md (preferred) or AGENTS.md, never both.

nodes.label: Domain Docs
nodes.rationale: Where CONTEXT.md and ADRs live plus consumer rules; defaults to single-context (one CONTEXT.md + docs/adr/), multi-context via CONTEXT-MAP.md only on monorepo signals.

nodes.label: Domain Docs Consumer Rules
nodes.rationale: Read CONTEXT.md / CONTEXT-MAP.md and docs/adr/ before exploring; proceed silently if absent — domain-modeling creates them lazily. Use the glossary's vocabulary and flag ADR conflicts.

nodes.label: ADR
nodes.rationale: Read ADRs that touch the area you're about to work in; if output contradicts an existing ADR, surface it explicitly rather than silently overriding.

nodes.label: GitHub Issue Tracker Template
nodes.rationale: gh CLI for all operations; GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs; PRs-as-request-surface flag defaults off.

nodes.label: Wayfinder Map
nodes.rationale: Map is a single issue labelled wayfinder:map with child tickets as sub-issues or task-list entries; frontier query, claim and resolve operations drive the wayfinder flow.

nodes.label: Blocking
nodes.rationale: Native issue dependencies (blocked_by via gh api, using database ids) are the canonical UI-visible representation; fall back to a 'Blocked by: #n' line. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.

nodes.label: GitLab Issue Tracker Template
nodes.rationale: glab CLI for all operations; GitLab numbers issues and MRs separately, so #42 is unambiguous; comments are called notes.

nodes.label: Wayfinder Map
nodes.rationale: Map is a single issue labelled wayfinder:map, or a native epic on tiers with epics; children carry 'Part of #<map>' and wayfinder:<type> labels.

nodes.label: Blocking
nodes.rationale: Native blocking links via the /blocked_by quick action are canonical but Premium/Ultimate-only; free tier falls back to a 'Blocked by: #n' line.

nodes.label: Local Markdown Issue Tracker Template
nodes.rationale: Issues and specs live as markdown files in .scratch/<feature-slug>/; one file per ticket, Status: line records triage state. Good for solo projects or repos without a remote.

nodes.label: Wayfinder Map
nodes.rationale: Map is .scratch/<effort>/map.md with one child file per ticket under issues/; Type: and Status: lines, Blocked by: lines, frontier scan and claim/resolve by file edits.

nodes.label: Blocking
nodes.rationale: 'Blocked by: NN, NN' line near the top; a ticket is unblocked when every file it lists is resolved.

nodes.label: Triage Labels
nodes.rationale: Canonical role names differ from actual tracker label strings; the right-hand column of the mapping is per-repo editable.

nodes.label: System Boundary Mocking
nodes.rationale: Mock only at system boundaries (external APIs, DBs, time/randomness, file system) - never your own classes, internal collaborators, or anything you control.

nodes.label: SDK-style Interfaces
nodes.rationale: Prefer SDK-style interfaces over generic fetchers: each mock returns one specific shape, no conditional logic in test setup, type safety per endpoint.

nodes.label: Test-Driven Development
nodes.rationale: The red->green loop only produces tests worth keeping when each section is consulted before and during the cycle, not after.

nodes.label: Seam
nodes.rationale: Test only at pre-agreed seams - no test is written at an unconfirmed seam; agreeing seams up front lands testing effort on critical paths instead of every edge case.

nodes.label: Red-Green Loop
nodes.rationale: Red before green, one slice at a time; don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.

nodes.label: TDD Anti-patterns
nodes.rationale: Horizontal slicing tests imagined behavior (the shape of things, not behavior), so work in vertical slices instead; tautological tests pass by construction so expected values must come from an independent source of truth.

nodes.label: Tracer Bullet
nodes.rationale: Each vertical-slice test is a tracer bullet that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

nodes.label: Good Tests
nodes.rationale: Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details; a good test reads like a specification and survives refactors.

nodes.label: Tautological Tests
nodes.rationale: Expected value restates the implementation so the test passes by construction; expected values must be independent known literals.

nodes.label: To Spec
nodes.rationale: No interview - just synthesize what you already discussed; use the project's domain glossary vocabulary and respect ADRs.

nodes.label: User Stories
nodes.rationale: A LONG numbered list of user stories - extremely extensive, covering all aspects of the feature.

nodes.label: Implementation Decisions
nodes.rationale: File paths and code snippets are omitted because they go stale fast; prototype snippets are inlined only when they encode a decision more precisely than prose.

nodes.label: To Tickets
nodes.rationale: Tickets are tracer-bullet vertical slices sized to fit a single fresh context window; granularity and blocking edges are quizzed with the user before publishing.

nodes.label: Blocking Edges
nodes.rationale: A ticket with no blockers can start immediately; blockers are published as native blocking links on a real tracker or as text in one file per ticket locally.

nodes.label: Wide Refactor
nodes.rationale: Blast radius fans across the whole codebase so no vertical slice can land green; the exception to vertical slicing - don't force it into a tracer bullet.

nodes.label: Expand-Contract
nodes.rationale: Expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks; migrate call sites in batches sized by blast radius keeping CI green; contract: delete the old form once no caller remains.

nodes.label: Agent Brief
nodes.rationale: Durability over precision - briefs must survive the issue sitting for days/weeks while the codebase changes; behavioral not procedural; complete, testable acceptance criteria so the agent knows when it's done; no file paths or line numbers.

nodes.label: Acceptance Criteria
nodes.rationale: Each criterion must be concrete, testable and independently verifiable - the agent needs to know when it's done.

nodes.label: Out-of-Scope Knowledge Base
nodes.rationale: Institutional memory plus deduplication: the reasoning survives the closed issue and similar requests surface the prior rejection instead of re-litigating; one file per concept, not per issue; only rejected enhancements (not bugs, not already-implemented).

nodes.label: Concept Similarity Matching
nodes.rationale: Matching is by concept similarity, not keyword - 'night theme' matches dark-mode.md; the maintainer confirms, reconsiders, or disagrees.

nodes.label: Triage
nodes.rationale: A PR is an issue with attached code - same roles, same states, same machine; every comment or issue posted during triage must start with the AI-generated disclaimer.

nodes.label: Ready-for-Agent
nodes.rationale: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent; moving an issue here requires posting an agent brief comment.

nodes.label: Grilling
nodes.rationale: Relentless one-question-at-a-time interview; a grilling agent that answers its own questions has broken HITL.

nodes.label: Domain Modeling
nodes.rationale: Sharpens domain terms and updates CONTEXT.md/ADRs inline as decisions land.

nodes.label: Wayfinder
nodes.rationale: Planning by default - the map is done when the way is clear; the pull to just do the work is usually the signal you've reached the edge of the map; refer to tickets by name, never bare ids.

nodes.label: Wayfinding Map
nodes.rationale: The map is an index, not a store - a decision lives in exactly one place (its ticket) so the map only gists and links; a single issue labelled wayfinder:map whose tickets are child issues.

nodes.label: Decision Ticket
nodes.rationale: Questions whose resolution is a decision, not slices of a build to execute; sized to one 100K token agent session; claims via assignment before any work.

nodes.label: Fog of War
nodes.rationale: Don't chart what you can't yet see - the map is deliberately incomplete; the 'Not yet specified' section graduates into tickets as the frontier advances; the test is whether you can state the question precisely now, not answer it.

nodes.label: Frontier
nodes.rationale: The open, unblocked, unclaimed children of the map - the edge of the known; blocking uses the tracker's native dependency relationship so the frontier renders visually.

nodes.label: Human In The Loop
nodes.rationale: A HITL ticket only resolves through a live exchange with a human who speaks for themselves - the agent never stands in for the human's side of it.

nodes.label: Research (Skill)
nodes.rationale: AFK ticket type: reading docs, third-party APIs, or knowledge bases to surface a fact a decision waits on; resolved by a /research subagent, fired in parallel.

nodes.label: Prototype (Skill)
nodes.rationale: HITL ticket type: raise the fidelity of the discussion with a cheap, rough, concrete artifact to react to; links the prototype as an asset.

nodes.label: In-Progress Skills Bucket
nodes.rationale: Skills still being developed - not ready to ship, expect rough edges and abandoned experiments; excluded from the plugin and top-level README until they graduate to a stable bucket.

nodes.label: Batch Grill Me
nodes.rationale: A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a later round, not this one; the session ends when the frontier is empty.

nodes.label: Design Tree
nodes.rationale: Every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it; finding facts is the agent's job, never the user's - dispatch sub-agents; decisions belong to the user.

nodes.label: Frontier (Batch Grill Me)
nodes.rationale: Every decision whose prerequisites are already settled - the questions you can ask now without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet; ask the whole frontier in one round.

nodes.label: Handoff Summary
nodes.rationale: Don't duplicate content already captured in other artifacts - reference by path or URL; redact sensitive information because the summary becomes the agent's prompt; include a suggested-skills section.

nodes.label: Background Agent
nodes.rationale: Launched via 'claude --bg' seeded with the handoff summary as its prompt; starts in the current working directory and returns immediately; user manages it with 'claude agents'.

nodes.label: Loop Me
nodes.rationale: A stateful /grilling session whose only output is workflow specs; mandate nothing structural - no AI, checkpoint, or schedule unless grilling shows it.

nodes.label: Loop
nodes.rationale: A recurring pattern in the user's life (career, week, morning, a single repeated activity); picturing life as loops within loops reveals how predictable activities are - which is what makes them worth delegating.

nodes.label: Workflow
nodes.rationale: The spec of one loop, made real - you run a workflow on a loop, the loop is its running instantiation; workflows live in workflows/*.md and are the source of truth; done when an implementer agent could build it without asking a single question.

nodes.label: Trigger
nodes.rationale: What fires each run: an event (a new email, a new issue) or a schedule (every morning); event-triggering is usually the more efficient.

nodes.label: Checkpoint
nodes.rationale: A human-in-the-loop point where the user is asked to verify or decide; some workflows have none and run autonomously, some use no AI at all.

nodes.label: Push Right
nodes.rationale: Defer the checkpoint as far as it will go - do maximal work before involving the human so they are asked once, late, with everything prepared; speed of review is imperative.

nodes.label: Brief
nodes.rationale: What a checkpoint presents: a tight, decision-ready summary - what was produced, why, and a link down to the asset itself, never the raw output; the user reads a brief, not a draft.

nodes.label: Setup TS Deep Modules agent config
nodes.norm_label: setup ts deep modules agent config

nodes.label: deep module
nodes.rationale: A lot of behaviour behind a small interface. Public vs private is decided by depth: anything in any subfolder is private, so the rule never needs extending to add a folder; packages are flat (one tier of immediate children) and may not nest packages.

nodes.label: entry points
nodes.rationale: The public surface is the package's root files, not one designated index.ts — several small entry points beat a giant barrel; adding an entry point is just adding a root file.

nodes.label: dependency-cruiser
nodes.rationale: Installed as a devDependency to enforce the four boundary rules (entry-point boundary, intra-package freedom, tests through entry points, no cycles); $1 back-references let a package reach its own internals while outsiders can't.

nodes.label: barrel files
nodes.rationale: Discouraged explicitly — keep entry points small and hide implementation in subfolders instead of re-exporting a whole subtree through one index.

nodes.label: recipient gap
nodes.rationale: Grill the send, not the subject: interview the user only about who it goes to and what they need back, which they can always answer; the questions in the document then target the gap between what the recipient knows and what the user needs.

nodes.label: grill the send, not the subject
nodes.norm_label: grill the send, not the subject

nodes.label: questionnaire template
nodes.rationale: Framed as a discovery questionnaire, most-important-first because async means you may only get one pass; every question is one idea, never compound, with an answer stub beneath.

nodes.label: bash wizard
nodes.rationale: A bash script that walks a human through a manual procedure tedious to do by hand and tedious to re-explain to an AI every time — opens URLs, captures values, writes .env and GitHub secrets, confirms at every stage. Ephemeral by default; commit only when the user wants a repeatable setup path.

nodes.label: template.sh
nodes.rationale: The delightful UX is already solved by template.sh (progress with time-remaining, confirmation gates, cross-platform URL opening, hidden secret entry, idempotent .env upserts, gh secret/variable writes, closing summary). The library above the STAGES marker is identical in every wizard — consistency is the point, never hand-edit it.

nodes.label: beat
nodes.rationale: One move in the journey that does one thing then stops, sized by what it needs (a sentence to several paragraphs). If a 'beat' needs five paragraphs and three subheadings, it's two beats glued together — split it.

nodes.label: grounding
nodes.rationale: Every concept must be grounded before a beat can lean on it; a beat that reaches for an ungrounded concept loses the reader — the one move the journey can't make. The unit is the concept, not the word for it. The big lever is what you make a prerequisite versus what you ground inside the piece.

nodes.label: choose-your-own-adventure journey
nodes.rationale: A candidate beat is only reachable if everything it requires is already grounded; picking a beat that grounds concept X unlocks every beat waiting on X. The article ends when the journey is complete — not when the pile is empty.

nodes.label: fragment
nodes.rationale: Any piece of text that might survive into the final article; it must be readable by the author but need not be comprehensible to a cold reader. Fragments are deliberately heterogeneous and separated by horizontal rules.

nodes.label: leading word
nodes.rationale: A compact metaphor or coinage the whole piece can hang on — the most valuable fragment to land; name the right one in explore and it shapes structure, transitions, and title through the entire exploit phase.

nodes.label: explore
nodes.rationale: Pure explore widens the space of what could be written without committing to structure — committing is exploit, a separate skill's job; imposing phases, outlines, or article structure is out of scope here.

nodes.label: novelist's diary
nodes.rationale: The model for fragments: years of unstructured noticings that later get mined for raw material — fragments are noticings.

nodes.label: exploit
nodes.rationale: The exploring is done, the pile is fixed — commit to a structure and mine the pile to fill it. The pile is a quarry, not a script: fragments may be split, merged, or paraphrased so the article reads as one voice.

nodes.label: grounding
nodes.rationale: A concept gets grounded as a prerequisite (before the opening, fixed at the start) or introduced (a block establishes it). The lever is what you make a prerequisite versus what you ground inside: demand too much up front shuts readers out; ground too much inside and the opening drowns in definitions.

nodes.label: format arguments
nodes.rationale: Weigh format tradeoffs out loud with the user, not silently: prose vs list (parallel items → list), inline vs callout (only if it genuinely derails the argument), table vs repeated structure (3+ repeats of same shape → table), quote vs paraphrase, code block vs inline code.

nodes.label: PreToolUse hook
nodes.rationale: Intercepts dangerous git commands before Claude executes them; when blocked, Claude sees a message saying it does not have authority to access these commands. Scope: this project (.claude/settings.json) or all projects (~/.claude/settings.json), merging into existing hooks.PreToolUse rather than overwriting.

nodes.label: shoehorn
nodes.rationale: Lets you pass partial data in tests while keeping TypeScript happy, replacing `as` assertions. Problems with `as`: trained against, must manually specify target type, needs double-as (`as unknown as Type`) for intentionally wrong data. Test code only — never in production.

nodes.label: fromPartial
nodes.rationale: Replaces `as Type` for large objects where only some properties matter — pass partial data that still type-checks.

nodes.label: fromAny
nodes.rationale: Replaces `as unknown as Type` for intentionally wrong data in error tests while keeping autocomplete.

nodes.label: fromExact
nodes.rationale: Forces a full object — a swap-in for fromPartial when you later want to require completeness.

nodes.label: sections
nodes.rationale: Directory naming: XX-section-name/ inside exercises/, XX.YY-exercise-name/ inside a section, dash-case. Use git mv (not mv) when renumbering to preserve git history.

nodes.label: problem/solution/explainer variants
nodes.rationale: problem/ is the student workspace with TODOs, solution/ is the reference implementation, explainer/ is conceptual material with no TODOs — default to explainer/ when stubbing unless the plan specifies otherwise.

nodes.label: lint rules
nodes.rationale: Validated by `pnpm ai-hero-cli internal lint`: subfolders must exist, readme.md non-empty with no broken links, no .gitkeep or speaker-notes.md, no `pnpm run exercise` commands, main.ts required per subfolder unless readme-only.

nodes.label: setup-pre-commit
nodes.rationale: Pre-commit runs lint-staged first (fast, staged-only), then full typecheck and tests. Husky v9+ needs no shebangs in hook files; `prettier --ignore-unknown` skips files Prettier can't parse. Detect package manager from lockfiles, default npm.

nodes.label: Semantic Design Language
nodes.rationale: DESIGN.md acts as the single source of truth for prompting Stitch: descriptive natural-language rules paired with precise values (hex codes, rem values) that Stitch's AI agent can interpret, instead of technical jargon

nodes.label: Anti-Pattern Bans (AI Tells)
nodes.rationale: Explicit 'NEVER DO' rules (no Inter font, no AI-purple neon, no emojis, no pure black) are what make the output premium - anti-patterns are as important as the rules themselves

nodes.label: Semantic Design Language
nodes.rationale: Translates battle-tested anti-slop frontend directives into Stitch's native semantic design language of Visual Descriptions with precise values

nodes.label: Design Approval Hard-Gate
nodes.rationale: No implementation until a design is presented and approved, even for 'simple' projects - unexamined assumptions in simple projects cause the most wasted work

nodes.label: Root Cause Investigation
nodes.rationale: Iron law: no fixes without root cause investigation first - random fixes waste time and create new bugs; symptom fixes are failure

nodes.label: Four-Phase Debugging Process
nodes.rationale: Root Cause, Pattern Analysis, Hypothesis and Testing, Implementation - each phase must complete before proceeding; systematic is faster than guess-and-check thrashing

nodes.label: Question the Architecture
nodes.rationale: After 3+ failed fixes, stop and question the architecture - repeated failures are not a failed hypothesis but a wrong architecture

nodes.label: Review Checkpoints
nodes.rationale: Stop and ask when blocked rather than guessing - review plan critically first, follow steps exactly, never skip verifications

nodes.label: Verify Tests Before Completion
nodes.rationale: Never present merge options or proceed with failing tests - merging broken code or creating failing PRs is the top mistake

nodes.label: Provenance-Based Worktree Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Only clean up worktrees the skill created (.worktrees/ or worktrees/); harness-owned workspaces must be left alone to avoid phantom state

nodes.label: Isolated Workspace
nodes.rationale: Detect existing isolation first, then prefer native platform tools, fall back to git worktrees only when needed - never fight the harness; using git worktree add with a native tool creates phantom state

nodes.label: Skill Invocation Rule
nodes.rationale: If there is even a 1% chance a skill applies, you MUST invoke it before any response or action - skills tell agents HOW to work, so skill check comes before clarifying questions

nodes.label: Process Skills Before Implementation
nodes.rationale: Process skills come first and set the approach, then implementation skills carry it out - e.g. brainstorming before 'let's build X', systematic-debugging before 'fix this bug'

nodes.label: Parallel Dispatch
nodes.rationale: One agent per independent problem domain, working concurrently - multiple dispatch calls in one response equal parallel execution; preserves controller context for coordination

nodes.label: Independent Problem Domains
nodes.rationale: Only parallelize when failures are independent with no shared state - related failures should be investigated together first

nodes.label: Bite-Sized Task Granularity
nodes.rationale: Each step is one 2-5 minute action with exact file paths, complete code, exact commands and expected output - plans assume an engineer with zero context and questionable taste

nodes.label: No Placeholders in Plans
nodes.rationale: TBD, 'add error handling', 'write tests for the above', and 'similar to Task N' are plan failures - repeat the code because the engineer may read tasks out of order

nodes.label: Verify Before Implementing
nodes.rationale: External feedback is suggestions to evaluate, not orders to follow - verify against codebase reality before implementing, push back with technical reasoning when wrong

nodes.label: No Performative Agreement
nodes.rationale: 'You're absolutely right!', 'Great point!', and gratitude expressions are forbidden - actions speak, technical correctness over social comfort

nodes.label: Review Early, Review Often
nodes.rationale: Dispatch a reviewer subagent to catch issues before they cascade - reviewer gets precisely crafted context, never the session history

nodes.label: TDD Applied to Documentation
nodes.rationale: Writing skills IS test-driven development applied to process documentation - no skill without a failing test first; if you didn't watch an agent fail without the skill, you don't know if it teaches the right thing

nodes.label: Skill Discovery Optimization
nodes.rationale: Descriptions that summarize a skill's workflow create a shortcut agents take - descriptions must state only triggering conditions ('Use when...') so agents read the full skill body

nodes.label: Bulletproofing Against Rationalization
nodes.rationale: Discipline skills need prohibition + rationalization tables + red flags to resist loopholes, but prohibitions backfire on shaping problems - recipes beat prohibitions for wrong-shaped output

nodes.label: Fresh Subagent Per Task
nodes.rationale: Delegating to specialized agents with isolated context preserves controller context and prevents context pollution between tasks

nodes.label: Task Review Gates
nodes.rationale: Each task gets a two-verdict review (spec compliance + code quality) after implementation, plus a broad whole-branch review at the end - review loops catch issues early, cheaper than debugging later

nodes.label: Durable Progress Ledger
nodes.rationale: Conversation memory does not survive compaction - controllers that lost their place re-dispatched entire completed task sequences; track progress in a ledger file, not only todos

nodes.label: Red-Green-Refactor
nodes.rationale: If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing - test-first forces edge case discovery before implementing, tests-after verify what you built not what's required

nodes.label: TDD Iron Law
nodes.rationale: No production code without a failing test first - write code before the test, delete it and start over; no exceptions

nodes.label: Evidence Before Claims
nodes.rationale: No completion claims without fresh verification evidence - if you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes; skipping any step is lying, not verifying

nodes.label: Root Cause Investigation
nodes.rationale: Iron law: no fixes without root cause investigation first - random fixes waste time and create new bugs; symptom fixes are failure

nodes.label: Four-Phase Debugging Process
nodes.rationale: Root Cause, Pattern Analysis, Hypothesis and Testing, Implementation - systematic debugging is faster than thrashing (15-30 min vs 2-3 hours, 95% vs 40% first-time fix rate)

nodes.label: The Three Dials
nodes.rationale: DESIGN_VARIANCE (8), MOTION_INTENSITY (6), VISUAL_DENSITY (4) gate every layout, motion and density decision - every rule is contextual and driven by these global variables, never invented aliases

nodes.label: Design Read (Brief Inference)
nodes.rationale: Most LLM design output is bad because the model jumps to a default aesthetic instead of reading the room - infer page kind, vibe, audience and quiet constraints before any code; state a one-line design read

nodes.label: AI Tells (Forbidden Patterns)
nodes.rationale: LLM defaults must be overridden proactively - the em-dash ban is the single most-violated tell; AI-purple gradients, three equal feature cards, Inter and beige+brass premium palettes are banned defaults

nodes.label: Pre-Flight Check
nodes.rationale: A 50+ item mechanical matrix run before outputting code - if a single checkbox cannot be honestly ticked, the page is not done

nodes.label: The Three Dials (v1)
nodes.rationale: Active baseline configuration strictly set to VARIANCE 8, MOTION 6, DENSITY 4 driving the logic of sections 3 through 7

nodes.label: Creative Arsenal
nodes.rationale: A library of advanced patterns (hero paradigms, bento grid, magnetic buttons, perpetual micro-interactions) pulled to avoid generic UI; GSAP/ThreeJS never mixed with Framer Motion in one tree

nodes.label: Red-Green-Refactor
nodes.rationale: If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing - tests written after code pass immediately, proving nothing

nodes.label: TDD Iron Law
nodes.rationale: No production code without a failing test first - write code before the test, delete it and start over; no exceptions

nodes.label: 99 UX Guidelines by Priority
nodes.rationale: Rule categories are ranked by priority (Accessibility and Touch/Interaction CRITICAL, then Performance, Style, Layout, Typography, Animation, Forms, Navigation, Charts) - follow priority 1 to 10 to decide which to focus on first

nodes.label: 5-Phase Pipeline
nodes.author: Mann-Makhecha
nodes.rationale: Workflow-driven rather than reference-driven: Ideation, Blueprint, Generation, Assembly, Deployment - each phase produces concrete deliverables before advancing from a raw idea to deployment-ready builds

nodes.label: unity-developer
nodes.rationale: Prioritizes performance optimization from project start, scalable architecture for teams, platform-first design decisions, and proactive profiling to identify bottlenecks.

nodes.label: unity-ecs-patterns
nodes.rationale: Data-oriented design rationale: cache-friendly entity storage with Jobs/Burst parallelization for thousands of entities; converting OOP game code to ECS to optimize CPU-bound logic.

nodes.label: Data-Oriented Technology Stack (DOTS)
nodes.rationale: Structure-of-arrays layout keeps entities in contiguous memory; the design intent behind DOTS is throughput over object orientation.

nodes.label: unreal-engine-cpp-pro
nodes.rationale: Performance first and GC safety by discipline: disable ticking by default, prefer timers, avoid Cast in hot loops, cache lookups outside Tick; trade-off is convention for robustness.

nodes.label: UObject hygiene
nodes.rationale: GC correctness requires every UObject* member wrapped in UPROPERTY; TStrongObjectPtr only for roots outside the UObject graph; IsValid() over nullptr to handle pending-kill state.

nodes.label: using-superpowers
nodes.rationale: Mandatory skill invocation before any response because undisciplined action wastes time; even a 1% chance a skill applies means invoke it to check.

nodes.label: skill invocation
nodes.rationale: Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any action or response; process skills (brainstorming, debugging) before implementation skills; rigid skills are followed exactly, flexible skills adapted.

nodes.label: Instruction priority
nodes.rationale: User explicit instructions > superpowers skills > default system prompt; skills override defaults where they conflict, but the user is always in control.

nodes.label: writing-plans
nodes.rationale: Assume the engineer has zero context and questionable taste: every task must be bite-sized, complete, self-contained; DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits.

nodes.label: implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Saved to docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature>.md with a mandatory header (goal, architecture, tech stack) and checkbox task tracking; plan document feeds an executor verbatim.

nodes.label: Bite-sized task granularity
nodes.rationale: Each step is one 2-5 minute action (write failing test, verify it fails, minimal implementation, verify pass, commit) so each change is independently reviewable.

nodes.label: No placeholders
nodes.rationale: TBD/TODO/"add validation" steps are plan failures because an executing agent will fill gaps wrongly or skip them; exact paths, complete code, and exact commands with expected output are required.

nodes.label: executing-plans (superpowers)
nodes.rationale: Inline execution option after a plan is saved; executes tasks in-session in batches with checkpoints for review, per the plan's REQUIRED SUB-SKILL header.

nodes.label: writing-skills
nodes.rationale: Skill creation IS TDD applied to process documentation: if you didn't watch an agent fail without the skill, you don't know it teaches the right thing; no skill without a failing test first.

nodes.label: SKILL.md frontmatter
nodes.rationale: Only name and description are required (max 1024 chars); name uses letters/numbers/hyphens; description is third-person, starts with "Use when...", describes ONLY triggering conditions.

nodes.label: TDD for documentation
nodes.rationale: RED (baseline pressure scenario without skill) to GREEN (minimal skill) to REFACTOR (close loopholes with rationalization tables and red flags); Iron Law applies to new skills and edits.

nodes.label: Claude Search Optimization (CSO)
nodes.rationale: Description = when to use, NEVER what the skill does; workflow summaries create a shortcut Claude follows instead of reading the skill body, so the body becomes documentation Claude skips.

nodes.label: test-driven-development (superpowers)
nodes.rationale: REQUIRED BACKGROUND: defines the RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle that writing-skills adapts to documentation; the same discipline applied to code is applied to skills.
